sections.title: Poetry about Hades and the Requirements for Courage

elements.context: τοσούτῳ ἧττον ἀκουστέον παισὶ καὶ ἀνδράσιν
φρίττειν δὴ ποιεῖ ὡς οἴεται πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας

signals.observation: Forms of ἀκούω recur throughout, framing the section: what must and must not be heard (ἀκουστέον τε καὶ οὐκ ἀκουστέον), what is pleasant to hear, what should less be heard, and the effect on those hearing.
An explicit inverse proportion: the more poetic something is, the less it should be heard by those who must be free.

elements.context: ἔχοντα ἐν αὑτῷ τοῦτο τὸ δεῖμα
τἀν Ἅιδου ἡγούμενον εἶναί τε καὶ δεινὰ εἶναι
ὀνόματα πάντα τὰ δεινά τε καὶ φοβερὰ

signals.observation: A cluster around fear and terribleness: δεδιέναι, δεῖμα, δεινά recur in connection with death and Hades.

elements.context: πρὸ ἥττης τε καὶ δουλείας θάνατον

signals.observation: δουλεία appears first as what the brave choose death over (slavery in battle), then returns as what the guardians must fear more than death (slavery of death-fear itself).
Four distinct verbs of erasure/removal accumulate: wiping out, striking through, casting away, taking away—each applied to poetic content about Hades.

elements.context: θερμότεροι καὶ μαλακώτεροι τοῦ δέοντος γένωνται

signals.observation: Shuddering (φρίκη, cold trembling) is said to make guardians hotter and softer—a paradoxical physical result from a cold stimulus.

elements.form: βουλοίμην κʼ ἐπάρουρος ἐὼν θητευέμεν ἄλλῳ

signals.observation: Achilles' speech from Odyssey 11 is the first quotation: preferring servitude on earth to ruling all the dead—servitude chosen over kingship in Hades.

elements.form: ψυχὴ καὶ εἴδωλον, ἀτὰρ φρένες οὐκ ἔνι πάμπαν
ψυχὴ δʼ ἐκ ῥεθέων πταμένη Ἄϊδόσδε βεβήκει
ψυχὴ δὲ κατὰ χθονός, ἠΰτε καπνός, ᾤχετο τετριγυῖα

signals.observation: The quoted passages present ψυχή as insubstantial—εἴδωλον without φρένες, shadows darting, flying from the body, going under earth like smoke squeaking.
τρίζω appears three times across two adjacent quotations—the squeaking of the soul-as-smoke and the squeaking of bat-souls in the cave.
Four underworld names are listed as the kind of terrible and fearful names (ὀνόματα δεινά τε καὶ φοβερά) that must be cast away; the names themselves perform the shuddering they are said to cause.

elements.context: ἡμεῖς δὲ ὑπὲρ τῶν φυλάκων φοβούμεθα

signals.observation: The speakers themselves fear (φοβούμεθα) on behalf of the guardians that the guardians might shudder (φρίττειν)—fear about fear.

elements.form: τὸν δὲ ἐναντίον τύπον τούτοις λεκτέον τε καὶ ποιητέον

signals.observation: The section opens with what must and must not be heard and closes with the demand that the opposite type (ἐναντίον τύπον) must be spoken and composed.

elements.context: τὸν δὲ ἐναντίον τύπον τούτοις λεκτέον

signals.observation: λέγω recurs across the section: what must be said, those who attempt to say, those who would not be saying truth, and what must be said instead.

elements.context: παραιτησόμεθα Ὅμηρόν τε καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους ποιητάς

signals.observation: The censors' stance toward poets is described through a sequence of supervisory but conciliatory actions: overseeing, requesting not to revile, begging pardon of Homer, asking him not to be angry.
Verbal adjectives in -τέον/-τέα cluster throughout, marking obligations: what must be heard, said, cast away, removed, spoken, composed.

sections.title: Lamentations, Uncontrolled Laughter, and Truth in Poetry

signals.observation: Forms of ὀδύρομαι/ὀδυρμός recur densely across the section, applied first to distinguished men, then to Achilles, then to gods, then to the unrestrained person who would sing laments.

elements.context: ἐξαιροῖμεν τοὺς θρήνους τῶν ὀνομαστῶν ἀνδρῶν

signals.observation: ἐξαιρέω appears first as a future indicative stating removal, then in a question about its correctness, then as an optative confirming the removal—shifting from proposal to justification.
Laments are removed from distinguished/notable men and reassigned to women (not serious ones) and bad men—a transfer with explicit contrast between recipients.

elements.context: ὁ τοιοῦτος μάλιστα αὐτὸς αὑτῷ αὐτάρκης πρὸς τὸ εὖ ζῆν

signals.observation: Triple αὐτ- cluster: αὐτὸς αὑτῷ αὐτάρκης, a striking phonetic and morphological concentration around self-sufficiency.
δεινόν recurs three times in close succession, each time negated or minimized for the ἐπιεικής man—death, suffering, loss each declared not δεινόν.
ἥκιστα appears three times consecutively, structuring a chain: least needs others → least terrible to lose → least laments.
Achilles' and Priam's bodies move through multiple positions—side, back, face-down, upright, wandering, rolling in dung—a dense cluster of bodily postures in grief.

elements.context: πολλοὺς ἐπὶ σμικροῖσιν παθήμασιν θρήνους ἂν ᾄδοι
ἄσβεστος δʼ ἄρʼ ἐνῶρτο γέλως μακάρεσσι θεοῖσιν

signals.observation: The section moves from prohibiting excessive lamentation to prohibiting excessive laughter—θρῆνος and γέλως placed in sequence as parallel excesses to be removed.

elements.context: ἰσχυρὰν καὶ μεταβολὴν ζητεῖ τὸ τοιοῦτον

signals.observation: ἰσχυρός appears twice in immediate adjacency: strong laughter seeks strong change—the adjective links the intensity of the emotion to the magnitude of its effect.
Falsehood is likened to a φάρμακον and restricted to ἰατροί/rulers—a medical semantic cluster governing the distribution of ψεῦδος.

elements.context: τοῖς δὲ ἄλλοις πᾶσιν οὐχ ἁπτέον τοῦ τοιούτου

signals.observation: ἁπτέον appears twice, both times negated for non-rulers—falsehood is something not to be touched by private persons, a tactile verb for a cognitive act.
Three expert-layperson pairs (doctor-patient, trainer-athlete, pilot-sailors) are listed as analogues to ruler-citizen in the matter of truthfulness.
νεώς appears first literally (a ship with a pilot) and then as a simile for the πόλις—the city as ship recurs within a few lines.

elements.context: ἀνθρώποις δὲ χρήσιμον ὡς ἐν φαρμάκου εἴδει

signals.observation: ἄχρηστον for gods versus χρήσιμον for humans—a μέν/δέ contrast built on the same root χρη- with opposing prefixes.

elements.context: ἕως ἄν τις ἡμᾶς ἄλλῳ καλλίονι πείσῃ

signals.observation: The λόγος is something one must obey (πειστέον) unless someone persuades (πείσῃ) with a finer one—πείθω in verbal adjective and subjunctive in adjacent clauses.
The section closes with the conditional that deeds (ἔργα) must follow upon the word (λόγῳ)—a λόγος/ἔργον pairing at the final line.

elements.context: ἑαυτόν γέ τις ἄνθρωπον ὄντα ἀνάξιον ἡγήσαιτο τούτων

signals.observation: Achilles is identified as θεᾶς παῖδα, yet the argument turns on the ordinary person (ἄνθρωπον ὄντα) who would consider himself unworthy of restraint if even a goddess's son laments.

sections.title: Temperance in Poetry and the Conclusion of the Content-Rules

elements.context: σωφροσύνης ἆρα οὐ δεήσει ἡμῖν τοῖς νεανίαις
σωφροσύνης δὲ ὡς πλήθει οὐ τὰ τοιάδε μέγιστα
εἴς γε σωφροσύνην νέοις ἐπιτήδεια ἀκούειν
Πηλέως, σωφρονεστάτου τε καὶ τρίτου ἀπὸ Διός

signals.observation: σωφροσύνη appears three times as a noun framing the discussion, then returns as the superlative adjective σωφρονεστάτου applied to Peleus in the characterization of Achilles' lineage.

elements.context: αὐτοὺς δὲ ἄρχοντας τῶν περὶ πότους καὶ ἀφροδίσια καὶ περὶ ἐδωδὰς ἡδονῶν

signals.observation: ἄρχων appears first as those to whom one is obedient, then as self-rule over pleasures, then as the target of insolent speech from private citizens—three distinct relations of ruling within a few lines.

elements.context: τῶν περὶ πότους καὶ ἀφροδίσια καὶ περὶ ἐδωδὰς ἡδονῶν
παρὰ πλεῖαι ὦσι τράπεζαι σίτου καὶ κρειῶν

signals.observation: The three pleasures named abstractly (drinking, sex, eating) at 389e are concretely instantiated in the Homeric quotations at 390b: full tables of food and meat, wine from the mixing-bowl, and death by hunger as its inversion.

elements.context: Ἄρεώς τε καὶ ἀφροδίτης ὑπὸ Ἡφαίστου δεσμόν

signals.observation: ἀφροδίσια first names a category of pleasure to be mastered, then appears as Zeus's overwhelming desire, then the proper name Ἀφροδίτη appears in the binding by Hephaestus—the abstract appetite becomes divine narrative.

elements.context: δῶρα θεοὺς πείθει, δῶρʼ αἰδοίους βασιλῆας
δῶρα μὲν λαβόντι ἐπαμύνειν τοῖς Ἀχαιοῖς
ἄνευ δὲ δώρων μὴ ἀπαλλάττεσθαι τῆς μήνιος

signals.observation: δῶρον appears five times in rapid succession: gifts persuade gods, gifts persuade kings, Phoenix advises accepting gifts, Achilles takes gifts from Agamemnon, and ransom for a corpse—all clustered around the prohibition on φιλοχρηματία.

elements.context: οὐ μὲν δὴ δωροδόκους γε ἐατέον εἶναι τοὺς ἄνδρας

signals.observation: φιλοχρήματος appears as a general prohibition, is then applied to Achilles, and intensifies into the noun φιλοχρηματία paired with ἀνελευθερία as one of two diseases in Achilles.

πείθω recurs densely across the section: gifts persuade gods; listeners must not be persuaded; we must not allow persuasion of our young; and one who is persuaded grants himself forgiveness—persuasion is both the danger and the mechanism being regulated.

elements.context: σιωπῇ ἧσο, ἐμῷ δʼ ἐπιπείθεο μύθῳ

signals.observation: Two Homeric quotations are placed in direct contrast: obedient silence addressed to a superior versus abusive address (dog-eyed, deer-hearted) from a private man to a ruler.
ἐγκράτεια (self-mastery) and καρτερία (endurance) name the positive capacity, while ἐπιθυμία names what overcomes Zeus—the section explicitly contrasts mastery and desire.

elements.form: στῆθος δὲ πλήξας κραδίην ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ

signals.observation: The approved Homeric example is a man striking his own chest and addressing his own heart with a command to endure—self-directed speech and self-directed physical action, unique among the quotations in the section.

Achilles is described as containing two diseases opposite to each other: servility-with-money-love and arrogance toward gods and men. The dual form νοσήματε δύο ἐναντίω ἀλλήλοιν is a striking formulation.

elements.context: περὶ γὰρ θεῶν ὡς δεῖ λέγεσθαι εἴρηται
οὐκοῦν καὶ περὶ ἀνθρώπων τὸ λοιπὸν εἴη ἄν

signals.observation: A fourfold descending sequence is enumerated: gods, daimons-and-heroes, those in Hades, humans—the first three are declared complete, the last is declared impossible to settle at present.

elements.context: ἀδύνατον δή, ὦ φίλε, ἡμῖν τοῦτό γε ἐν τῷ παρόντι τάξαι
ἡ δὲ δικαιοσύνη ἀλλότριον μὲν ἀγαθόν, οἰκεία δὲ ζημία

signals.observation: The section's final movement declares it impossible now (ἀδύνατον ἐν τῷ παρόντι) to legislate about humans until justice is discovered—the content-rules are explicitly suspended pending the finding of what justice is.
The poets' claim is stated as a chiastic contrast: unjust but happy, just but wretched—this is what the current discussion cannot yet refute.

elements.context: μηδέ τινʼ ἄλλον θεοῦ παῖδά τε καὶ ἥρω
Ἀχιλλεύς, θεᾶς ὢν παῖς καὶ Πηλέως

signals.observation: Divine parentage recurs insistently: child of a goddess, child of a god, near-sown of gods, children of gods, gods beget evils—the logic forces a disjunction: either the deeds are not theirs or they are not gods' children.

sections.title: Narration and Mimesis: The Form of Poetry

elements.context: δύο μιμήματα δύνανται οἱ αὐτοὶ ἅμα εὖ μιμεῖσθαι
μιμητικοὺς ἡμῖν δεῖ εἶναι τοὺς φύλακας

signals.observation: The μιμ- word family (μίμησις, μιμέομαι, μίμημα, μιμητικός, μιμητής, ἀφομοίωμα) saturates the section, appearing in nearly every phase of the discussion.

elements.context: οὐκ ἂν μίμησις ἦν ἀλλὰ ἁπλῆ διήγησις

signals.observation: διήγησις first appears as a general term covering all poetic speech, then is qualified as ἁπλῆ (simple) in contrast to mimetic narration, and finally appears as a small residual element in the speech of the inferior type.

elements.context: εἰ ἄρα μανθάνω ἃ σὺ λέγεις

signals.observation: μανθάνω recurs as Adeimantus' repeated failure and eventual success in understanding, and then Socrates uses it of himself at 396b, reversing the direction of comprehension.

elements.context: τὰ μὲν δὴ λόγων πέρι ἐχέτω τέλος
τὸ δὲ λέξεως μετὰ τοῦτο σκεπτέον

signals.observation: The section opens with an explicit division: λόγοι (content) is declared finished; λέξις (manner of expression) is announced as the new topic.

elements.form: ἃ μὲν λεκτέον ἤδη εἰρῆσθαι, ὡς δὲ λεκτέον ἔτι σκεπτέον
ἅ τε γὰρ λεκτέον καὶ ὡς λεκτέον εἴρηται

signals.observation: The pairing λεκτέον / ὡς λεκτέον is restated at 394c as partially complete, then at the section's close (398b) both are declared finished.

elements.context: γελοῖος ἔοικα διδάσκαλος εἶναι καὶ ἀσαφής
φράσω δὲ ἄνευ μέτρου· οὐ γάρ εἰμι ποιητικός

signals.observation: Socrates twice disclaims competence—as a teacher (γελοῖος, ἀσαφής) and as a poet (οὐ γάρ εἰμι ποιητικός)—while proceeding to demonstrate both teaching and recomposition.

elements.context: εἰ δέ γε μηδαμοῦ ἑαυτὸν ἀποκρύπτοιτο ὁ ποιητής
ὁμοιοῦν αὐτὸν τὴν αὑτοῦ λέξιν ἑκάστῳ

signals.observation: Mimesis is defined through the poet's self-concealment (ἀποκρύπτοιτο) and self-assimilation (ὁμοιοῦν) to another; these two actions together constitute the mimetic act.

elements.context: ἅπασα διὰ μιμήσεως φωναῖς τε καὶ σχήμασιν
κατὰ σῶμα καὶ φωνὰς καὶ κατὰ τὴν διάνοιαν

signals.observation: φωνή and σχῆμα appear paired as the media of mimetic likening at 393c, then return at 397b; at 395d φωνή is joined instead with σῶμα and διάνοια as domains where mimesis settles into habit.

elements.form: κυνῶν καὶ προβάτων καὶ ὀρνέων φθόγγους

signals.observation: A dense cluster of animal and natural sounds—neighing, lowing, rushing, crashing, thunder, dogs, sheep, birds—catalogues what the inferior mimetic poet will imitate.
The choice among poets is framed as ἄκρατος (unmixed) versus κεκραμένος (mixed), a mixing metaphor applied to styles of speech.

elements.form: προσκυνοῖμεν ἂν αὐτὸν ὡς ἱερὸν καὶ θαυμαστὸν καὶ ἡδύν
μύρον κατὰ τῆς κεφαλῆς καταχέαντες καὶ ἐρίῳ στέψαντες

signals.observation: The versatile poet is honored as sacred (ἱερόν), anointed with myrrh and crowned with wool, then sent away—reverence and expulsion performed together.

elements.form: εἰς ἔθη τε καὶ φύσιν καθίστανται
elements.context: αἱ μιμήσεις ἐὰν ἐκ νέων πόρρω διατελέσωσιν εἰς ἔθη τε καὶ φύσιν καθίστανται

signals.observation: Mimesis practiced from youth (ἐκ νέων) is said to settle into ἔθη (habits) and φύσις (nature), across body, voice, and thought.
ἐλευθερία and its opposites cluster: guardians are δημιουργοὶ ἐλευθερίας, should imitate ἐλευθέρους characters, and avoid τὰ ἀνελεύθερα.

elements.context: τόν τε σκυτοτόμον σκυτοτόμον εὑρήσομεν καὶ οὐ κυβερνήτην
τὸν γεωργὸν γεωργὸν καὶ οὐ δικαστήν
τὸν πολεμικὸν πολεμικὸν καὶ οὐ χρηματιστήν

signals.observation: A triple structure repeats each craft term twice (σκυτοτόμον σκυτοτόμον, γεωργὸν γεωργὸν, πολεμικὸν πολεμικὸν), each paired with a denied second occupation, enacting the one-person-one-craft principle in the syntax itself.
The accepted poet is αὐστηρότερος and ἀηδέστερος; the rejected mimetic poet is ἥδιστος. Pleasure (ἡδύς) belongs to the one who is expelled.

elements.form: ὅπῃ ἂν ὁ λόγος ὥσπερ πνεῦμα φέρῃ, ταύτῃ ἰτέον

signals.observation: Socrates compares the argument to a πνεῦμα (wind/breath) that carries them where it will, disclaiming foreknowledge of where the inquiry leads.

elements.context: ἡ μὲν διὰ μιμήσεως ὅλη ἐστίν
ἡ δὲ δι᾽ ἀπαγγελίας... ἐν διθυράμβοις
ἡ δ᾽ αὖ δι᾽ ἀμφοτέρων ἔν τε τῇ τῶν ἐπῶν ποιήσει

signals.observation: A threefold classification of poetry by mode: wholly mimetic (tragedy/comedy), wholly narrative (dithyramb), and mixed (epic).

elements.form: ἐνιστάναι εἰς τοὺς τῶν κακιόνων τύπους

signals.observation: The decent man's reluctance to imitate inferior characters is described with ἐκμάττειν (to mold/stamp oneself) and ἐνιστάναι εἰς τύπους (to set oneself into molds)—concrete craft metaphors for mimetic formation.

elements.context: πρέπουσαν ἁρμονίαν καὶ ῥυθμὸν τῇ λέξει

elements.form: πασῶν μὲν ἁρμονιῶν, πάντων δὲ ῥυθμῶν

signals.observation: The simple style requires one ἁρμονία and a near-uniform ῥυθμός; the mimetic style requires all harmonies and all rhythms—singularity versus multiplicity in musical terms.

elements.context: τὸ μέλος ἐκ τριῶν ἐστιν συγκείμενον, λόγου τε καὶ ἁρμονίας καὶ ῥυθμοῦ
τὸν πόδα τῷ τοῦ τοιούτου λόγῳ ἀναγκάζειν ἕπεσθαι καὶ τὸ μέλος, ἀλλὰ μὴ λόγον ποδί τε καὶ μέλει

signals.observation: μέλος is first named as composed of three elements (λόγος, ἁρμονία, ῥυθμός), then returns in the assertion that foot and μέλος must follow λόγος, not λόγος follow them.

elements.context: τήν γε ἁρμονίαν καὶ ῥυθμὸν ἀκολουθεῖν δεῖ τῷ λόγῳ
τὸ τῆς εὐσχημοσύνης τε καὶ ἀσχημοσύνης τῷ εὐρύθμῳ τε καὶ ἀρρύθμῳ ἀκολουθεῖ
τὸ εὔρυθμόν γε καὶ τὸ ἄρρυθμον τὸ μὲν τῇ καλῇ λέξει ἕπεται
ὁ τρόπος τῆς λέξεως καὶ ὁ λόγος οὐ τῷ τῆς ψυχῆς ἤθει ἕπεται
εὐλογία ἄρα καὶ εὐαρμοστία καὶ εὐσχημοσύνη καὶ εὐρυθμία εὐηθείᾳ ἀκολουθεῖ

signals.observation: ἀκολουθέω and ἕπομαι recur densely through a chain of following-relations: harmony/rhythm follow λόγος, εὐσχημοσύνη follows εὔρυθμον, εὔρυθμον follows καλὴ λέξις, λέξις follows ψυχῆς ἦθος, and the εὐ- cluster follows εὐήθεια.
Five εὐ- compounds are gathered in a single sentence, culminating in εὐήθεια which is then immediately disambiguated from its pejorative sense (ἄνοια).

elements.context: ἣν ἄνοιαν οὖσαν ὑποκοριζόμενοι καλοῦμεν ὡς εὐήθειαν

elements.form: εὖ τε καὶ καλῶς τὸ ἦθος κατεσκευασμένην διάνοιαν

signals.observation: εὐήθεια is explicitly split between a colloquial euphemism for ἄνοια and a literal meaning: a mind (διάνοια) whose ἦθος is well constructed.

elements.form: ἐν εἰρηνικῇ τε καὶ μὴ βιαίῳ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἑκουσίᾳ πράξει

signals.observation: The two retained harmonies are paired as βίαιον/ἑκούσιον, corresponding to πολεμική πρᾶξις and εἰρηνική πρᾶξις, and further paired with δυστυχούντων/εὐτυχούντων and ἀνδρείων/σωφρόνων.

elements.context: οὐκ οἶδα, ἔφην ἐγώ, τὰς ἁρμονίας

elements.form: σὸν ἔργον, ὥσπερ τὰς ἁρμονίας, φράσαι

signals.observation: Socrates disclaims technical knowledge of harmonies and rhythms, deferring to Glaucon as μουσικός and to Damon, while nonetheless specifying the criteria the retained modes must satisfy.
Glaucon laughs and declares himself outside everyone (ἐκτὸς τῶν πάντων) in ability to contribute, just before being addressed as the musical expert.
πολυ- and παν- compounds cluster densely around the instruments to be excluded, marking excess of strings and modes.

elements.context: κρίνοντες τὸν Ἀπόλλω καὶ τὰ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος ὄργανα πρὸ Μαρσύου τε καὶ τῶν ἐκείνου ὀργάνων

signals.observation: The choice of lyre over aulos is framed as choosing Apollo and his instruments over Marsyas and his — named as a judgment (κρίνοντες) already made.

elements.context: λελήθαμέν γε διακαθαίροντες πάλιν ἣν ἄρτι τρυφᾶν ἔφαμεν πόλιν
ἴθι δή καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ καθαίρωμεν

signals.observation: διακαθαίροντες describes what has been happening unnoticed (λελήθαμεν), and καθαίρωμεν immediately follows as a deliberate exhortation to continue purging.

elements.context: λύρα δή σοι καὶ κιθάρα λείπεται καὶ κατὰ πόλιν χρήσιμα
καὶ αὖ κατʼ ἀγροὺς τοῖς νομεῦσι σῦριγξ

signals.observation: The surviving instruments are distributed spatially: lyre and kithara in the city, syrinx in the fields for herdsmen.

elements.context: πολλὰ ἑκάστης ἡμέρας κατὰ σμικρὸν ἀπὸ πολλῶν δρεπόμενοί τε καὶ νεμόμενοι

elements.form: αὔρα φέρουσα ἀπὸ χρηστῶν τόπων ὑγίειαν

signals.observation: Bad environment is figured as grazing on toxic pasture (κακῇ βοτάνῃ, δρεπόμενοι, νεμόμενοι); good environment as dwelling in a healthy place with a breeze carrying health from good places.

elements.form: καταδύεται εἰς τὸ ἐντὸς τῆς ψυχῆς
elements.context: μάλιστα καταδύεται εἰς τὸ ἐντὸς τῆς ψυχῆς ὅ τε ῥυθμὸς καὶ ἁρμονία
ἀπὸ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἢ πρὸς ὄψιν ἢ πρὸς ἀκοήν τι προσβάλῃ

signals.observation: Rhythm and harmony are said to sink inward (καταδύεται εἰς τὸ ἐντός) into the soul, while the beautiful strikes (προσβάλῃ) toward sight or hearing from outside.

elements.context: τὰ στοιχεῖα μὴ λανθάνοι ἡμᾶς ὀλίγα ὄντα ἐν ἅπασιν οἷς ἔστιν περιφερόμενα
εἰκόνας γραμμάτων, εἴ που ἢ ἐν ὕδασιν ἢ ἐν κατόπτροις ἐμφαίνοιντο
τὰ τῆς σωφροσύνης εἴδη καὶ ἀνδρείας καὶ ἐλευθεριότητος καὶ μεγαλοπρεπείας

signals.observation: The analogy moves from recognizing letters (στοιχεῖα) and their images in water and mirrors to recognizing the εἴδη of virtues and their images — the same structure of original and εἰκών applied to literacy and then to moral perception.

elements.context: ὁ δὲ ὀρθὸς ἔρως πέφυκε κοσμίου τε καὶ καλοῦ σωφρόνως τε καὶ μουσικῶς ἐρᾶν

signals.observation: The coincidence of beautiful character and form is called κάλλιστον θέαμα, immediately linked to ἐρασμιώτατον, and then ὀρθὸς ἔρως is defined as loving what is κόσμιον and καλόν σωφρόνως and μουσικῶς.

elements.context: τέλος ἡμῖν ἔχειν ὁ περὶ μουσικῆς λόγος
δεῖ δέ που τελευτᾶν τὰ μουσικὰ εἰς τὰ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐρωτικά

signals.observation: The section closes by declaring that μουσική must end (τελευτᾶν) in τὰ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐρωτικά — τέλος, τελευτᾶν, and τετελεύτηκεν cluster at the closing.

elements.context: ἀσχημοσύνη καὶ ἀρρυθμία καὶ ἀναρμοστία κακολογίας καὶ κακοηθείας ἀδελφά
τοῦ ἐναντίου, σώφρονός τε καὶ ἀγαθοῦ ἤθους, ἀδελφά τε καὶ μιμήματα

signals.observation: ἀδελφά is used to name kinship relations: first between ἀσχημοσύνη-cluster and κακοήθεια, then between their opposites and good ἦθος, then again for the sister-virtues at 402c.

elements.context: ἕν τι συνιστάντες λανθάνωσιν κακὸν μέγα ἐν τῇ αὑτῶν ψυχῇ
εὐθὺς ἐκ παίδων λανθάνῃ εἰς ὁμοιότητά τε καὶ φιλίαν καὶ συμφωνίαν τῷ καλῷ λόγῳ ἄγουσα

signals.observation: λανθάνω recurs three times: guardians unknowingly accumulating evil, the breeze unknowingly leading youth toward harmony, and letters not escaping notice — hiddenness operating in opposed directions.

sections.title: Gymnastics for Guardians and Its Parallel to Simple Music

elements.context: ὃ ἂν χρηστὸν ᾖ σῶμα, τοῦτο τῇ αὑτοῦ ἀρετῇ ψυχὴν ἀγαθὴν ποιεῖν
ψυχὴ ἀγαθὴ τῇ αὑτῆς ἀρετῇ σῶμα παρέχειν ὡς οἷόν τε βέλτιστον

signals.observation: The expected direction (good body producing good soul) is denied; the actual direction is reversed—good soul produces the best possible body.

elements.context: ἀδελφή τις ἂν εἴη τῆς ἁπλῆς μουσικῆς
ἡ δὲ ἁπλότης κατὰ μὲν μουσικὴν ἐν ψυχαῖς σωφροσύνην, κατὰ δὲ γυμναστικὴν ἐν σώμασιν ὑγίειαν

signals.observation: ἁπλοῦς/ἁπλότης recurs three times, first linking gymnastics to simple music as siblings, then as the abstract noun producing σωφροσύνη and ὑγίεια in the concluding formulation.
ποικιλία first names Sicilian culinary variety, then returns as the agent that engenders ἀκολασία and νόσος, contrasted with ἁπλότης.

elements.context: ἐκεῖ μὲν ἀκολασίαν ἡ ποικιλία ἐνέτικτεν
κατὰ μὲν μουσικὴν ἐν ψυχαῖς σωφροσύνην
κατὰ δὲ γυμναστικὴν ἐν σώμασιν ὑγίειαν

signals.observation: A fourfold parallel: ποικιλία yields ἀκολασία (soul) and νόσος (body); ἁπλότης yields σωφροσύνη (soul) and ὑγίεια (body).

elements.context: ἡ βελτίστη γυμναστικὴ ἀδελφή τις ἂν εἴη τῆς ἁπλῆς μουσικῆς

signals.observation: The best gymnastics is called a sister (ἀδελφή) of simple music, a kinship term applied to the relation between two educational domains.

elements.context: ὑπνώδης αὕτη γέ τις καὶ σφαλερὰ πρὸς ὑγίειαν
ὥσπερ κύνας ἀγρύπνους τε ἀνάγκη εἶναι

signals.observation: Sleep and wakefulness cluster: professional athletes are characterized as sleepy (ὑπνώδης, καθεύδουσι), while guardians must be sleepless (ἀγρύπνους) like dogs.

elements.context: ὥσπερ κύνας ἀγρύπνους τε ἀνάγκη εἶναι

signals.observation: Guardians are compared to dogs (κύνας), with the simile specifying wakefulness, sharp sight and hearing.

elements.context: κομψοτέρας δή τινος ἀσκήσεως δεῖ τοῖς πολεμικοῖς ἀθληταῖς

signals.observation: Professional athletes' regimen (ἀσκηταί) is rejected for the warrior-athletes (πολεμικοῖς ἀθληταῖς), who need a more refined (κομψοτέρας) training.
The phrase φύλακα φύλακος—a guardian needing a guardian—is marked as γελοῖον; the same noun in two cases creates a reflexive absurdity.

elements.context: οὔτε ἑφθοῖς κρέασιν ἀλλὰ μόνον ὀπτοῖς
οὐδὲ μὴν ἡδυσμάτων Ὅμηρος πώποτε ἐμνήσθη
Συρακοσίαν δέ, ὦ φίλε, τράπεζαν καὶ Σικελικὴν ποικιλίαν ὄψου
Ἀττικῶν πεμμάτων τὰς δοκούσας εἶναι εὐπαθείας

signals.observation: A dense cluster of specific foods and cuisines: Homer's heroes eat only roasted meat, no fish, no seasonings; Syracusan tables, Sicilian variety-dishes, Corinthian companions, and Attic pastries are all rejected.

elements.form: μελοποιίᾳ τε καὶ ᾠδῇ τῇ ἐν τῷ παναρμονίῳ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι ῥυθμοῖς πεποιημένῃ

elements.context: ὅλην γὰρ οἶμαι τὴν τοιαύτην σίτησιν καὶ δίαιταν

signals.observation: Elaborate diet (σίτησις καὶ δίαιτα) is explicitly likened (ἀπεικάζοντες) to song composed in the panharmonic mode and in all rhythms—dietary variety is mapped onto musical variety.

elements.context: δεῖ μὲν δὴ καὶ ταύτῃ ἀκριβῶς τρέφεσθαι ἐκ παίδων διὰ βίου

signals.observation: θρεπτέοι and τρέφεσθαι (both from τρέφω) frame the transition to gymnastics: the young men must be nourished/reared in it. τύπους signals that only outlines will be given, deferring detailed specification to the trained διάνοια.

elements.context: ψέγεις ἄρα καὶ Κορινθίαν κόρην φίλην εἶναι ἀνδράσιν μέλλουσιν εὖ σώματος ἕξειν

signals.observation: Κορινθίαν κόρην (a Corinthian girl, i.e. courtesan) is placed among dietary luxuries as something to be censured for men who intend bodily fitness—sexual indulgence listed alongside food items.

elements.context: ὅτι μάλιστα ὀξὺ ὁρᾶν καὶ ἀκούειν
πολλὰς μεταβολὰς ἐν ταῖς στρατείαις μεταβάλλοντας

signals.observation: The guardian's required capacities form a cluster of sensory sharpness (ὀξὺ ὁρᾶν καὶ ἀκούειν), endurance of change (μεταβολάς… μεταβάλλοντας), and resistance to instability (μὴ ἀκροσφαλεῖς)—contrasted with the athletes' fragility.

sections.title: Courts, Medicine, and the City: The Lesson of Asclepius and Herodicus

elements.context: δικαστήριά τε καὶ ἰατρεῖα πολλὰ ἀνοίγεται

signals.observation: Courts and medical establishments are paired as institutions that open, then their corresponding arts (δικανική, ἰατρική) are paired as becoming honored; the pairing recurs throughout the section.
Forms of αἰσχρός accumulate in escalating degrees (αἰσχρόν, αἴσχιστον, αἴσχιον, αἰσχρόν) across successive questions about shameful dependence on courts and doctors.
The litigious man is described through a dense cluster of twisting/turning language: turning every turn, traversing every passage, twisting away, wrestling—a physical vocabulary for legal evasion.
The dozing judge (νυστάζοντος δικαστοῦ) is a striking image: the person one should not need is presented as drowsy.
Bodies filling up like marshes with flows and winds—a water/air image cluster for disease caused by idleness and diet, forcing the Asclepiads to invent new disease names.

The claim that such diseases didn't exist under Asclepius is supported by a concrete Homeric scene: his sons at Troy gave Eurypylus Pramnian wine with barley and cheese—foods called φλεγματώδη—without censure.

elements.context: ἀπέκναισε πρῶτον μὲν καὶ μάλιστα ἑαυτόν
ἀποκναιόμενος εἴ τι τῆς εἰωθυίας διαίτης ἐκβαίη

signals.observation: ἀποκναίω appears first as active (Herodicus wore out himself), then as middle/passive (being worn out by departing from his habitual regimen)—the same verb turns reflexive.

elements.context: δυσθανατῶν δὲ ὑπὸ σοφίας εἰς γῆρας ἀφίκετο

signals.observation: Herodicus is said to have made his death long (μακρὸν τὸν θάνατον) and to have died with difficulty (δυσθανατῶν) by means of his expertise (ὑπὸ σοφίας)—σοφία produces a prolonged dying.

elements.context: ὁ δὲ δὴ πλούσιος οὐδὲν ἔχει τοιοῦτον ἔργον

signals.observation: The carpenter who is sick demands quick treatment or accepts death because he has work (ἔργον); the rich man has no such ἔργον compelling him, creating a contrast between productive necessity and idle luxury.

elements.context: οὐ γὰρ οἶμαι σώματι σῶμα θεραπεύουσιν
δικαστὴς δέ γε ψυχῇ ψυχῆς ἄρχει

signals.observation: A three-step asymmetry: doctors treat body with soul (not body with body); the judge rules soul with soul. The instrument shifts from ψυχῇ σῶμα to ψυχῇ ψυχῆς, and θεραπεύω shifts to ἄρχει.

elements.context: οὐκ ἔχοντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς παραδείγματα ὁμοιοπαθῆ τοῖς πονηροῖς
πρὸς τὰ ἐν αὑτῷ παραδείγματα ἀποσκοπῶν

signals.observation: παράδειγμα recurs three times: the decent lack inner patterns matching the wicked; the cunning man looks to his own inner patterns; and when among the good he lacks a pattern of goodness.
The good judge knows injustice through ἐπιστήμη, not through personal ἐμπειρία οἰκεία—knowledge versus firsthand experience is explicitly contrasted.

elements.context: οὐκ οἰκείαν ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ ψυχῇ ἐνοῦσαν

signals.observation: The good judge perceives injustice not as οἰκεία (one's own, dwelling in his own soul) but as ἀλλοτρία ἐν ἀλλοτρίαις (alien in alien souls)—a pointed own/alien contrast.

elements.context: πονηρία μὲν γὰρ ἀρετήν τε καὶ αὑτὴν οὔποτʼ ἂν γνοίη
ἀρετὴ δὲ φύσεως παιδευομένης χρόνῳ ἅμα αὑτῆς τε καὶ πονηρίας ἐπιστήμην λήψεται

signals.observation: An asymmetry: πονηρία can never know ἀρετή or itself; ἀρετή, educated over time, will acquire knowledge of both itself and πονηρία.

elements.context: εἰ μὲν θεοῦ ἦν, οὐκ ἦν αἰσχροκερδής· εἰ δʼ αἰσχροκερδής, οὐκ ἦν θεοῦ

signals.observation: A disjunctive argument about Asclepius: if son of a god, not base-profiting; if base-profiting, not son of a god—structured as a chiastic denial rejecting the tragic poets and Pindar.

elements.context: οὐ σχολὴ κάμνειν οὐδὲ λυσιτελεῖ οὕτω ζῆν
εἰ μὴ πράττοι, οὐκ ἐλυσιτέλει ζῆν
οὔτε αὐτοῖς οὔτε τοῖς ἄλλοις ᾤοντο λυσιτελεῖν ζῆν

signals.observation: λυσιτελέω recurs across different subjects: the carpenter judges life not worth living without work; Asclepius judges prolonged treatment not profitable for the person or the city; and the sons of Asclepius judge it not profitable to treat the intemperate.

elements.context: οὐδενὶ σχολὴ διὰ βίου κάμνειν ἰατρευομένῳ
ἐν ἀσχολίᾳ τε πάντων ἰατρευόμενος διὰ βίου ἔζη

signals.observation: σχολή and its negation ἀσχολία cluster around being sick: no one has leisure to be sick through life; the carpenter has no leisure to be sick; Herodicus lived his whole life in the busyness of being treated.

elements.context: ὅσοι μὲν κατὰ σῶμα τοιοῦτοι, ἀποθνῄσκειν ἐάσουσιν
τοὺς δὲ κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν κακοφυεῖς καὶ ἀνιάτους αὐτοὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν

signals.observation: A graduated distinction: those incurable in body will be allowed to die; those incurable in soul will be actively killed by the judges themselves.
Glaucon characterizes Asclepius as πολιτικόν and his sons as κομψούς—both are the interlocutor's responsive epithets applied to the medical figures.

sections.title: The Purpose of Music and Gymnastics for the Soul

elements.context: πρὸς τὸ θυμοειδὲς τῆς φύσεως βλέπων κἀκεῖνο ἐγείρων
εἴ τι θυμοειδὲς εἶχεν, ὥσπερ σίδηρον ἐμάλαξεν
ἐὰν δὲ θυμοειδῆ, ἀσθενῆ ποιήσας τὸν θυμὸν
ἐπὶ τὸ θυμοειδὲς καὶ τὸ φιλόσοφον

signals.observation: θυμοειδής recurs densely across the section, first as what gymnastics should awaken, then as what music softens like iron, then as what is replaced by ἀκράχολοι καὶ ὀργίλοι, and finally as one of the two targets of the two arts.
Two paired qualities are set out as a fourfold contrast: ἀγριότης/σκληρότης versus μαλακία/ἡμερότης, corresponding to excess gymnastics versus excess music.

elements.context: ἀμφότερα τῆς ψυχῆς ἕνεκα τὸ μέγιστον καθιστάναι

signals.observation: The claim that both music and gymnastics are established for the sake of the soul corrects the common opinion (οὐχ οὗ ἕνεκά τινες οἴονται) that one serves body and the other soul.

elements.context: τοῦ μὲν ἡρμοσμένου σώφρων τε καὶ ἀνδρεία
τοῦ δὲ ἀναρμόστου δειλὴ καὶ ἄγροικος

signals.observation: The ἁρμόζω family appears in five forms spanning attunement of the two natures, the harmonized versus unharmonized soul, their joint tuning, and the superlative εὐαρμοστότατον.

elements.context: τὸ δὴ μετὰ τοῦτο ἤδη τήκει καὶ λείβει

elements.form: ἐκτέμῃ ὥσπερ νεῦρα ἐκ τῆς ψυχῆς

signals.observation: A metallurgical-corporeal cluster describes music's excessive effect: softening like iron, then melting, dissolving, and cutting sinews from the soul.

elements.form: χρήσιμον ἐξ ἀχρήστου καὶ σκληροῦ ἐποίησεν

signals.observation: Music first makes the spirited element useful from useless and hard, but continued excess produces a μαλθακὸν αἰχμητήν — a soft spearman.

elements.context: καταχεῖν τῆς ψυχῆς διὰ τῶν ὤτων

signals.observation: καταυλεῖν and καταχεῖν, both with κατα- prefix, describe music being piped down and poured down into the soul through the ears as through a funnel (χώνη).

elements.form: ὀρθῶς μὲν τραφὲν ἀνδρεῖον ἂν εἴη
μᾶλλον δʼ ἐπιταθὲν τοῦ δέοντος σκληρόν τε καὶ χαλεπὸν γίγνοιτʼ ἄν

signals.observation: The spirited element rightly nurtured becomes ἀνδρεῖον, but overstretched beyond τοῦ δέοντος becomes σκληρόν τε καὶ χαλεπόν — a parallel conditional structure.

elements.form: ἀσθενές τε καὶ κωφὸν καὶ τυφλὸν
οὐκ ἐγειρόμενον οὐδὲ τρεφόμενον οὐδὲ διακαθαιρομένων τῶν αἰσθήσεων

signals.observation: The φιλομαθές in the soul of the exclusive gymnast becomes weak, deaf, and blind, because it is neither awakened, nourished, nor its perceptions cleansed.

elements.form: πειθοῖ μὲν διὰ λόγων οὐδὲν ἔτι χρῆται
βίᾳ δὲ καὶ ἀγριότητι ὥσπερ θηρίον

signals.observation: The exclusive gymnast no longer uses persuasion through speech but acts by force and savagery like a beast — πειθώ/λόγος contrasted with βία/ἀγριότης/θηρίον.

elements.context: συναρμοσθῆτον ἐπιτεινομένω καὶ ἀνιεμένω μέχρι τοῦ προσήκοντος

signals.observation: The dual ἐπιτεινομένω καὶ ἀνιεμένω (tightening and loosening) applies string-tuning language to the two parts of the soul.

elements.context: τοῦτον ὀρθότατʼ ἂν φαῖμεν εἶναι τελέως μουσικώτατον
πολὺ μᾶλλον ἢ τὸν τὰς χορδὰς ἀλλήλαις συνιστάντα

signals.observation: The truly μουσικώτατον person is redefined as the one who blends gymnastics with music for the soul, explicitly distinguished from one who tunes strings (χορδάς).

elements.context: δύο τέχνα θεὸν ἔγωγʼ ἄν τινα φαίην δεδωκέναι

signals.observation: A god is said to have given two arts for two parts — θυμοειδές and φιλόσοφον — explicitly not for soul and body, correcting the earlier common opinion.
τοῦ δέοντος appears three times marking the threshold of excess in different directions — too savage, too hard, too soft.

elements.form: τύποι τῆς παιδείας τε καὶ τροφῆς
elements.context: οἱ μὲν δὴ τύποι τῆς παιδείας τε καὶ τροφῆς οὗτοι ἂν εἶεν

signals.observation: The section closes by declaring these the τύποι of education, and dismissing dances, hunts, gymnastic contests, and horse-racing as obvious consequences not requiring further discussion.
ἐγείρω appears first as the active awakening of the spirited element through gymnastics, then as the negated passive — the learning-loving part not being awakened in the exclusive gymnast.

sections.title: Selection of Rulers and the Noble Lie

elements.context: εἰ φυλακικοί εἰσι τούτου τοῦ δόγματος
ὁ σιδηροῦς φύλαξ ἢ ὁ χαλκοῦς φυλάξῃ

signals.observation: The φύλαξ/φυλακ- family is densely present throughout: from selecting the best guardians, to being guardians of a dogma, to being a guardian of oneself, to the renamed complete guardians vs. auxiliaries, to the myth's iron or bronze guardian destroying the city.

elements.context: πρῶτον μὲν αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἄρχοντας πείθειν
τοῖς οὖν ἄρχουσι καὶ πρῶτον καὶ μάλιστα παραγγέλλει ὁ θεός

signals.observation: ἄρχω/ἄρχων moves from a question about who will rule and be ruled, through selection criteria, to installation as ruler, to the myth where the god commands the rulers.
Three ways true opinion is lost involuntarily are named as a triad: theft, sorcery, and force. Each is then separately elaborated.

γοητεύω and its family recur from the initial test condition through the elaboration of sorcery as enchantment by pleasure or fear, the contest of sorcery for the young, and the desired quality of being hard to bewitch.

elements.context: βασανίζοντας πολὺ μᾶλλον ἢ χρυσὸν ἐν πυρί
ἐν ἀνδράσι βασανιζόμενον καὶ ἀκήρατον ἐκβαίνοντα

signals.observation: βασανίζω appears twice: first in a simile comparing testing of guardians to assaying gold in fire, then describing the man tested through every age who emerges ἀκήρατον (unalloyed/pure).

elements.context: βασανίζοντας πολὺ μᾶλλον ἢ χρυσὸν ἐν πυρί
χρυσὸν ἐν τῇ γενέσει συνέμειξεν αὐτοῖς

signals.observation: χρυσός first appears in a simile of testing gold by fire, then reappears as the metal mixed into rulers' souls at birth, then in the possibility of gold offspring from silver parents, then as the compound ὑπόχρυσος.

elements.context: σίδηρον δὲ καὶ χαλκὸν τοῖς τε γεωργοῖς

signals.observation: A cluster of four metals (gold, silver, iron, bronze) is introduced as divine mixture, then repeated with ὑπο- compound adjectives for mixed offspring, then as adjectives for the guardian who would destroy the city.

elements.context: ἑκουσίως μὲν ἡ ψευδὴς τοῦ μεταμανθάνοντος
τῶν ψευδῶν τῶν ἐν δέοντι γιγνομένων

signals.observation: ψεῦδος/ψευδής first names the false opinion voluntarily abandoned, then reappears as the necessary falsehood, then the noble lie (γενναῖόν τι ἓν ψευδομένους), then what Socrates is ashamed to speak.
The lie is described both as γενναῖον (noble) and as Φοινικικόν (Phoenician), the latter said to have happened often before according to poets but not in Socrates' time.

elements.form: ὑπὸ γῆς ἐντὸς πλαττόμενοι καὶ τρεφόμενοι
ἡ γῆ αὐτοὺς μήτηρ οὖσα ἀνῆκεν

signals.observation: The myth involves formation under the earth, the earth as mother sending them up (ἀνῆκεν), the land as both mother and nurse, and citizens as earthborn (γηγενῶν) brothers.

elements.context: ὥς φασιν οἱ ποιηταὶ καὶ πεπείκασιν
ἐπιχειρήσω πρῶτον μὲν αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἄρχοντας πείθειν
τοῦτον οὖν τὸν μῦθον ὅπως ἂν πεισθεῖεν

signals.observation: πείθω and πειθώ cluster densely around the introduction of the noble lie: persuading by the lie, poets having persuaded, requiring much persuasion, attempting to persuade rulers first, and asking how they might be persuaded.
Opinion exits the mind either voluntarily or involuntarily; false opinion departs voluntarily (through relearning), all true opinion departs involuntarily (ἄκοντες).

elements.form: ὥσπερ τοὺς πώλους ἐπὶ τοὺς ψόφους τε καὶ θορύβους ἄγοντες σκοποῦσιν εἰ φοβεροί

signals.observation: The testing of young guardians is compared to leading colts toward noises and tumults to see if they are fearful.

elements.context: κήδοιτο δέ γʼ ἄν τις μάλιστα τούτου ὃ τυγχάνοι φιλῶν
τῆς πόλεώς τε καὶ ἀλλήλων κήδεσθαι

signals.observation: κηδεμών/κήδομαι appears at the start as a requirement for rulers (caring for the city), is linked to loving (φιλῶν), and returns at the end where the myth promotes caring for city and one another.

elements.form: ἐν τε παισὶ καὶ νεανίσκοις καὶ ἐν ἀνδράσι

signals.observation: The testing spans all ages: first stated generally (ἐν ἁπάσαις ταῖς ἡλικίαις), then specified as boys, youths, and men.

elements.context: τοὺς δὲ νέους ... ἐπικούρους τε καὶ βοηθοὺς τοῖς τῶν ἀρχόντων δόγμασιν

signals.observation: The term φύλακες is split: the elder tested rulers become φύλακας παντελεῖς, while those previously called guardians are renamed ἐπικούρους τε καὶ βοηθούς.

elements.context: ὥσπερ ὀνείρατα ἐδόκουν ταῦτα πάντα πάσχειν
ἦσαν δὲ τότε τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ὑπὸ γῆς ἐντὸς πλαττόμενοι

signals.observation: The myth reframes education and upbringing as dreams (ὀνείρατα), while the truth (τῇ ἀληθείᾳ) is that they were being shaped underground—within a narrative explicitly called a ψεῦδος.
πλάττω appears for the forming of citizens underground and for the god fashioning them with different metals.

sections.title: The Guardians' Encampment and Way of Life

signals.observation: στρατοπεδεύομαι appears three times: first as the guardians' task of finding a camp, then as completed encampment before sacrifice, then as a simile for their permanent communal life.
Socrates draws an explicit contrast between military and money-making dwellings.
λύκος first names the external enemy attacking a flock, then names what the guardian-dogs themselves may become.
A dense cluster of shepherd/flock vocabulary within a short span.

elements.context: τοιούτους γε καὶ οὕτω τρέφειν κύνας

signals.observation: The guardians are called κύνας (dogs) who may become like wolves—the ἀντί construction marks the transformation.

elements.context: ἀντὶ συμμάχων εὐμενῶν δεσπόταις ἀγρίοις ἀφομοιωθῶσιν

signals.observation: The ἀντί + contrast pattern (allies vs. masters) appears at 416b and returns at 417b with varied wording.

elements.context: τούς τε ἔνδον μάλιστʼ ἂν κατέχοιεν

signals.observation: The inside/outside pair ἔνδον–ἔξωθεν frames the guardians' dual function at 415e and returns at 417b where the inside threat now exceeds the outside.

elements.context: ἅπτεσθαι χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου οὐ θέμις

signals.observation: Gold and silver accumulate densely from 416e–417a, named repeatedly in connection with prohibition.

elements.context: θεῖον παρὰ θεῶν ἀεὶ ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ ἔχουσι

signals.observation: Divine gold in the soul is contrasted with human/mortal gold; θεῖον–ἀνθρώπειος–θνητός form a graded contrast.
A cluster of pollution/purity and sacred-law language: μιαίνειν, ἀκήρατον, ἀνόσια, οὐ θέμις.

elements.context: τὰς οἰκήσεις καὶ τὴν ἄλλην οὐσίαν

signals.observation: οἴκησις recurs four times across the section, each time specifying or constraining the guardians' dwelling.

elements.form: σῴζοιντό τʼ ἂν καὶ σῴζοιεν τὴν πόλιν

signals.observation: The two possible outcomes are set in direct contrast: σῴζω (saving themselves and the city) versus running nearest to ὄλεθρος.

elements.form: γῆν τε ἰδίαν καὶ οἰκίας καὶ νομίσματα κτήσονται

signals.observation: Private property (ἰδίαν + κτάομαι) is first prohibited and then projected as the condition of ruin.
The guardians are called γηγενεῖς (earth-born) near the section's start; private γῆ is what they must not acquire near its end.
Two active-passive participle pairs in immediate sequence: hating/hated, plotting/plotted-against.
A prescribed sequence of actions: arm, advance, survey, encamp, sacrifice, make beds.
